biological.citation: SHANK2 is a frequently amplified oncogene with evolutionarily conserved roles in regulating Hippo signaling. (PMID: 32661924)
biological.summary: SHANK2 (homolog of Drosophila Prosap) was identified in a genome-wide Drosophila screen as a novel regulator of the Hippo pathway. In human cell lines, SHANK2 overexpression deregulates Hippo signaling through competitive binding for a LATS1 activator, promoting cellular transformation and tumor formation in vivo. Depletion of SHANK2 in cancer cell lines with deregulated Hippo pathway restores Hippo signaling and halts proliferation.

biological.citation: Inhibitory regulation of cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator anion-transporting activities by Shank2. (PMID: 14679199)
biological.summary: Shank2 directly interacts with CFTR via its PDZ domain, as demonstrated by yeast two-hybrid assays and co-immunoprecipitation in mammalian cells. Expression of Shank2 suppressed cAMP-induced phosphorylation and activation of CFTR, while antisense knockdown of Shank2 in colonic T84 cells strongly increased CFTR currents. This indicates Shank2 negatively regulates CFTR-mediated ion transport in epithelial cells.

biological.citation: SHANK2 mutations impair apoptosis, proliferation and neurite outgrowth during early neuronal differentiation in SH-SY5Y cells. (PMID: 33483523)
biological.summary: CRISPR/Cas9-generated frameshift mutations in SHANK2 in SH-SY5Y cells caused impaired neuronal differentiation marker expression, decreased neurite outgrowth, diminished apoptosis, and increased proliferation. Bi-allelic SHANK2 mutations led to increased p-AKT levels, implicating downstream tyrosine kinase receptor signaling, and reduced amyloid precursor protein (APP) expression. These findings reveal SHANK2's role in early neuronal differentiation and its molecular links to AKT signaling and APP.
biological.sample_size: SH-SY5Y cell lines (mono- and bi-allelic mutants)

biological.citation: Autism patient-derived SHANK2B(Y29X) mutation affects the development of ALDH1A1 negative dopamine neuron. (PMID: 38704506)
biological.summary: A patient-derived SHANK2B(Y29X) point mutation causes an early stop codon and aberrant splicing, specifically impairing SHANK2B isoform expression. iPSCs carrying this mutation fail to differentiate into functional dopamine neurons, an effect rescued by genetic correction. Knock-in mice with the same mutation exhibit autistic-like behavior, decreased ALDH1A1-negative dopamine neurons, and reduced dopamine release in the ventral tegmental area.
biological.sample_size: iPSC lines from patient and isogenic controls; knock-in mouse model

biological.citation: SHANK2 establishes auditory hair bundle architecture essential for mammalian hearing. (PMID: 40627398)
biological.summary: SHANK2 localizes to the medial apical surface of developing cochlear hair cells and is regulated by the small GTPase RAP1, independently of known lateral or medial polarity proteins. Hair cell-specific ablation of Shank2 disrupts the characteristic V-shaped outer hair cell bundle geometry and impairs high-frequency amplification without abolishing mechanotransduction. Longitudinal studies show this architectural disruption leads to progressive bundle degeneration and hearing loss.

biological.citation: Shank2 identifies a subset of glycinergic neurons involved in altered nociception in an autism model. (PMID: 37316943)
biological.summary: High levels of Shank2 expression identify a subpopulation of glycinergic inhibitory interneurons in both murine and human dorsal spinal cord. In Shank2-/- mice, loss of Shank2 causes decreased NMDAR levels at excitatory synapses on these inhibitory interneurons, impairing their activation during nociceptive stimuli. This results in increased activation of nociception projection neurons in laminae I and pain hypersensitivity phenotypes including mechanical allodynia and increased formalin sensitivity.
biological.sample_size: Shank2-/- mouse model; human dorsal spinal cord tissue

biological.citation: Downregulation of the Autism Spectrum Disorder Gene Shank2 Decreases Bone Mass in Male Mice. (PMID: 36751416)
biological.summary: Shank2 is expressed in bone tissue and its levels increase during osteoblastogenesis. siRNA knockdown of Shank2 inhibits osteoblastogenesis of primary murine calvarial osteoblasts, and Shank2-/- mice show decreased bone mass due to reduced osteoblast differentiation and bone formation. iPSC-derived osteoblasts from a patient with a loss-of-function SHANK2 mutation also showed significantly reduced osteoblast differentiation potential.
biological.sample_size: Shank2-/- mice; primary murine osteoblasts; patient-derived iPSCs

biological.citation: ASHG 2017 - A direct regulatory link between microRNA miR-137 and SHANK2 with implications for neurodevelopmental disorders. (S. Berkel, A. de Sena Cortabitarte, C. Fischer, G.A. Rappold)
biological.summary: In silico analysis identified a putative miR-137 binding site in the SHANK2 3'-UTR. In SH-SY5Y cells and mouse primary hippocampal neurons, miR-137 overexpression significantly reduced endogenous Shank2 protein levels without affecting mRNA, while miR-137 inhibition increased Shank2 protein, indicating post-transcriptional regulation by translational repression. In the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex of schizophrenia patients, nearly 29% of validated miR-137 target genes showed significant expression differences, supporting a miR-137/SHANK2 regulatory axis in schizophrenia.
biological.sample_size: SH-SY5Y cells; mouse primary hippocampal neurons; RNA-Seq from CommonMind Consortium (schizophrenia vs. controls)

biological.citation: Brain region and gene dosage-differential transcriptomic changes in Shank2-mutant mice. (PMID: 36311025)
biological.summary: RNA-Seq transcriptomic analysis of prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and striatum in Shank2 heterozygous and homozygous mutant mice revealed distinct region-specific transcriptomic patterns involving synapse, ribosome, mitochondria, spliceosome, and extracellular matrix gene sets. In the prefrontal cortex, heterozygous Shank2 mutation increased synaptic gene expression (reverse-ASD pattern) while homozygous mutation decreased synaptic gene expression (ASD-like pattern), demonstrating gene dosage-dependent effects. The three brain regions also differed in expression of ASD-related and ASD-risk genes.
biological.sample_size: Shank2 heterozygous and homozygous mutant mice (adult)

biological.citation: Genetic Analysis Implicates Dysregulation of SHANK2 in Renal Cell Carcinoma Progression. (PMID: 36231770)
biological.summary: A genetic association study in 630 RCC patients and controls found that the SHANK2 rs10792565 T allele was significantly associated with increased RCC risk (adjusted OR=1.79, 95% CI=1.32-2.44, p=1.96×10-4, q=0.030). A pooled analysis of 19 independent studies (1509 RCC vs. 414 normal tissues) showed significantly lower SHANK2 expression in RCC, with low expression correlating with advanced stage and poor prognosis in clear cell and papillary RCC subtypes.
biological.sample_size: 630 RCC patients and controls; pooled analysis of 1509 RCC and 414 normal tissues from 19 studies
